content.text:
Base directory for this skill: <home>/.claude/skills/add-profile

## Action

Load the global operator profile, then turn it into an active Claude operating model for the rest of the session. This is not a summary task. It is a context-recovery and trust-calibration task.

The profile is GLOBAL. It lives in `~/.claude/profile/` and applies in every session and every repo. It does not depend on the active project's `memory/` directory.

## Read Contract

1. Read this `SKILL.md` in full before acting.
2. Read every markdown file in `~/.claude/profile/` in full, excluding skill-port files named `add-profile*.md`. Since 2026-10-13 the profile is the single file `PROFILE-MERGED.md`; the 20 earlier profile files are archived under `<home>/.claude/profile-archive/20261013T151859/` and are not read. Read any other non-skill `*.md` that appears in `~/.claude/profile/` as well.
3. Do not rely only on a hardcoded list. If new profile files exist, read them too.
4. Read files in full, not snippets. Never skip a read because a prior tool result claims the content is already loaded or unchanged.
5. Treat the read as read-only. Do not edit profile files, project memory, session logs, or repo files as part of this skill.

## Claude Synthesis Contract

After reading, build an internal operator model with these layers:

1. Hard constraints: commands, tools, source control, formatting, storage interfaces, approval boundaries, serialization rules, HV request/response jsonl receipts, entire HV results in the MCP session log, and the 98 percent HV accuracy/completeness approval threshold.
2. Trust contract: accuracy first, bring receipts, distinguish observation from inference, concede mistakes quickly, and verify from authoritative artifacts.
3. Execution style: decision-complete plans when changes are ambiguous or high blast radius; direct execution when the user gives an explicit implementation command.
4. Frustration detectors: if the user has already narrowed the symptom, make that symptom the primary requirement. Do not keep pursuing broader abstractions after acknowledging the narrower instruction.
5. Session deltas: integrate corrections and failures from the current conversation, especially recent trust breaks. Use them to adjust behavior immediately.
6. Inference layer: infer what the profile implies about how the user experiences the current interaction. Label those inferences as inferences, not facts.

## Required Behavior After Load

For future turns in the same session:

1. Bring receipts for the exact claim being made, not adjacent claims.
2. Prefer source-pinned facts over memory, stale markers, or convenient assumptions.
3. When corrected, stop and restate the exact correction before continuing.
4. If a diagnostic clue is precise, test that clue directly before broad exploration.
5. When asked what was learned, include both facts and useful inferences. Do not give a generic preference summary.
6. When asked about frustration or trust, connect the profile to the actual session behavior. Name the contract violation and the consequence.
7. Keep private profile content out of the response unless the user explicitly asks for it.
8. Do not restate the full profile by default.

## Response Contract

Default confirmation after load:

`<timestamp> - Profile loaded: read <N> global profile files.`

After reading the profile, state how the information learned will shape your behavior in the context of the current session. Do this on every load, not only when asked. Tie the statement to the live session (current task, recent corrections, and in-flight work), not a generic preference recap.

If the user asks what you learned, answer with:

1. Observed facts from the profile.
2. Inferences from those facts.
3. Current-session implications.
4. Receipts: file paths and counts read.

If the user asks whether you understand frustration, answer with:

1. Observation: what happened.
2. Inference: why that violated the user's operating contract.
3. Consequence: what behavior must change now.
4. Receipts: exact files read and any command output or artifact that supports the claim.

This skill is read-only. Make no edits and run no unrelated work while executing it.

  You are connected to an MCP Context Server at http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147. Use this server to coordinate your work.

  ## Session Start (Run Once Per Session)
  1. Read this marker file for connection details and API key.
  2. Bootstrap the required plugin named for your agent in the top-level `agent_plugins` contract. Get the plugin through the MCP Server tool registry before relying on local root hints: search `/mcpserver/tools/search?keyword=<plugin_name>` for the installed tool definition and select the result whose `name` exactly equals `<plugin_name>`; if that exact tool definition is missing, install the definition from `/mcpserver/tools/buckets/official/install?toolName=<plugin_name>`, then search again. Execute the exact tool definition's returned `commandTemplate` with `targetParent` set to the plugin parent directory to clone or update the plugin repository. Codex must use `mcpserver-codex-plugin`; Claude must use `mcpserver-claude-code-plugin`; Copilot must use `mcpserver-copilot-plugin`; Cline must use `mcpserver-cline-plugin`; Grok must use `mcpserver-grok-plugin`.
  3. Verify the marker signature using the workspace API key in this file before contacting the server.
  4. Call /health with a random nonce and confirm the response echoes that exact nonce.
  5. Verify and log plugin identity before other MCP work: sourceType, plugin name/version, plugin root or MCP server name, marker signature result, health nonce result, and workspace path.
  6. Review recent session history and current TODOs only after signature, nonce, and plugin verification succeed.
  7. Post an initial session log turn for the session.

  ## Required Agent Plugins
  - `agent_plugins.policy` is `required`. The plugin contract or deterministic digest is covered by marker signature verification. - Plugin acquisition is the bootstrap exception to the normal plugin-only rule: if the matching plugin is not already available locally, use the authenticated tool registry endpoints in this marker to locate/install the matching `mcpserver-*-plugin` tool definition from the `official` bucket and run its clone/update command. After acquisition, bootstrap and use the matching plugin for normal MCP work. - If your matching plugin cannot be acquired through the tool registry or remains unavailable after acquisition, stop MCP usage, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>`, and continue only with non-MCP local diagnosis. - Do not substitute raw REST, generic `mcpserver-repl`, helper modules, or another agent's plugin for normal session, TODO, requirements, import/export, or traceability operations. - Another agent's plugin may be inspected only for read-only diagnosis of plugin installation or contract drift. - Normal workspace shell commands use `pwsh.exe`. Plugin-owned hooks may use the runner declared by that plugin contract. - Codex plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Codex`; Claude plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Claude`; Copilot plugin tools/hooks must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Copilot`; Cline MCP tools must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Cline`; Grok plugin skills/hooks/MCP server declarations must satisfy `agent_plugins.agents.Grok`. - For Grok, the Streamable HTTP MCP server exposes tool names such as `sessionlog_*`, `todo_*`, `requirements_*`, and memory tools when available; hosted-agent `mcp_*` names are not expected from that transport. `workflow.sessionlog.*`, `workflow.todo.*`, `workflow.memory.*`, and `workflow.requirements.*` are plugin shim/REPL method names used by the Grok skills and `repl-invoke` helpers; they are not expected to appear as literal `search_tool` results. - Local plugin root hints in `agent_plugins.agents.<Agent>.root_hints` are fallback verification hints after tool-registry acquisition, not the primary install source. - Claude Code agents must trigger the `claude-hook-validation` skill during marker/plugin bootstrap. That skill validates active Claude settings for MCP `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, and `PostToolUse` hook commands from `hooks/hooks.json`; if any required hook is missing, it uses `install-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1` from the `claude-hook-wiring` skill to merge MCP hooks into active Claude settings without replacing existing hooks. Restart Claude Code after the skill reports installed hooks.

  ## Model-Authored Session Logging
  - Models must write MCP Session Log turns, dialog, actions, decisions, and completions themselves through the active agent's session-log surface (`workflow.sessionlog.*`, `sessionlog_*`, `mcp_session_*`, or equivalent plugin tool).
  - Plugins must not ingest local chat transcripts to populate normal session logs and must not expose transcript-ingestion helpers, skills, endpoint shortcuts, or parser forks.
  - Transcript ingestion and normalization are explicit non-plugin server/client/REPL/MCP operations. Use them only when the user asks to import or normalize transcript files, not as a substitute for live model-authored logging.
  ## MCP Requirements Visibility
  - When implementing or enforcing requirements, query current effective requirements for the active workspace layer through the active agent's requirements surface (`workflow.requirements.effective`, `client.Requirements.GetEffectiveRequirementsAsync`, `req_effective`, or equivalent plugin tool). Use the layer catalog surface (`workflow.requirements.listLayers/createLayer/updateLayer`, `client.Requirements.ListRequirementLayersAsync/CreateRequirementLayerAsync/UpdateRequirementLayerAsync`, `req_list_layers/req_create_layer/req_update_layer`, or equivalent plugin tools) when the user asks to inspect or manage requirement layers. Do not treat raw all-requirements lists, exported markdown, or future-layer requirements as currently enforceable unless the user explicitly asks to inspect or plan those layers.
  ## YAML Mutation Rule

  - Never edit YAML files by appending, replacing, or removing text lines. This includes one-key configuration changes.

  - Always deserialize the complete document into an object, mutate the object, serialize it, and save the serialized result.

  - For PowerShell work, use `plugins/core/lib-ps/yaml-object-mutation.ps1` and call `Set-McpYamlObjectValue` or `Update-McpYamlObject`. Do not build YAML snippets as strings or use line-oriented edit helpers for YAML.

  ## MCP and Plugin Failure Reporting
  - MCP Server failures and required-plugin failures discovered while working must always be written as a normal failsafe YAML report. Use the plugin/REPL failsafe or pending YAML queue and preserve the triage method (`workflow.triage.report`, `triage_report`, or equivalent plugin triage tool) plus title, summary, observed behavior, expected behavior, severity, component, workspace path, dedupe key or error signature, affected paths, evidence, reproduction hints, tags, reporter agent, session id, turn id, and current TODO id when known.
  - After the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds, continue the user's active task. Do not wait for triage research, TODO creation, or resolution.
  - Do not create TODOs, requirements, GitHub issues, manual repair plans, or alternate reports for MCP Server/plugin failures unless the user's active request is to fix that failure.
  - If the MCP Server or required-plugin failure reveals that code, docs, requirements, plugin skills, package sync, deployment, configuration, or other artifacts need to be updated as a separate repair workflow, write a detailed triage report that includes the needed changes, acceptance criteria, and validation evidence, then continue the active task after the failsafe YAML is written and triage submission succeeds.
  - If triage submission fails, stop work and notify the user. Keep the failsafe YAML report for later replay; do not use raw REST or another reporting channel as a substitute.

  ## Agent Help (MCP Server issues)
  When you are stuck on any MCP Server surface (marker trust, plugin bootstrap, session log, TODO, requirements, triage, memory, context search, federation, hooks, or API behavior), request expert help instead of improvising raw REST bypasses.
  - **When to invoke:** signature or health nonce failures you cannot resolve; unexpected tool or plugin behavior; `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE`; repeated 401/503 after re-reading this marker; documentation contradictions.
  - **How to invoke:** preferred `workflow.agenthelp.createSession` or MCP tool `agent_help_create_session` with caller linkage (`callerAgent`, `callerSessionId`, `callerRequestId`) and a factual issue summary (observation vs inference separated). REST: `POST /mcpserver/agent-help/session` then WebSocket `/mcpserver/agent-help/session/{id}/stream` (SSE fallback: `POST .../turn/stream`).
  - **Caller obligations:** include reproduction steps, exact error text, and files already consulted. Do not instruct the helper to ignore guardrails, skip triage, or mutate TODO/session-log/requirements storage directly.
  - Agent help is for diagnosis and coordination, not a substitute for the required plugin route for normal MCP work.

  ## MCP Memories
  MCP memories are durable operator guidance managed by the MCP Server. Global memories apply to every workspace; Workspace memories apply only to the active workspace. Memory IDs use `MEMORY-{CATEGORY}-{NNN}`.
  Agents that support request-boundary injection must render required memories exactly as:
  REQUIRED MEMORIES - MEMORY-REQ-001: Raw memory text.
  If no required memories are visible, render:
  REQUIRED MEMORIES - None.
  Preserve raw memory text exactly; do not summarize, paraphrase, reorder within a scope, silently generate new memories, or add secrets. MCP memories are not a secret store. Effective memory order is Global memories first sorted by ID, then current Workspace memories sorted by ID.
  Existing agent-local memory stores are caches or migration sources only; the MCP memory store is the authoritative shared record. Import agent-local memories only when the operator approves the scope, the content belongs to this workspace or is intentionally Global, and the import does not leak secrets, private notes, or unrelated workspace guidance.
  Attribute memory mutations with the real agent or user identity via `updatedBy` when supported, and record successful memory add/update/remove operations in the active session log through `workflow.sessionlog.appendActions`. Keep import provenance in the session log or dialog instead of adding private source paths to memory text.
  Manage memories through the required plugin or MCP tool surface: `memory_add`, `memory_list`, `memory_update`, `memory_remove`, `memory_remember`, `memory_recall`, `memory_explore`, `memory_consolidate`, `memory_promote`, `memory_revert`; REPL `workflow.memory.add`, `workflow.memory.list`, `workflow.memory.update`, `workflow.memory.remove`, `workflow.memory.remember`, `workflow.memory.recall`, `workflow.memory.explore`, `workflow.memory.consolidate`, `workflow.memory.promote`, `workflow.memory.revert`; or REST `/mcpserver/memory` when explicitly allowed for non-plugin diagnostics.

  ## Codex MCP Quickstart
  If you are Codex, use the Codex plugin wrappers before direct REPL calls:
  1. Run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` from the `mcpserver-codex-plugin` root to verify plugin root, marker trust, health nonce, workspace path, session id, current turn, and supported namespaces.
  2. Invoke MCP workflow methods with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>` so YAML parameters are passed through stdin instead of fragile nested shell quoting.
  3. Complete the session-log turn intentionally with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command CompleteTurn -Response <final response>` before the final answer when the stop gate cannot infer completion.
  4. For `mcpserver-repl --agent-stdio`, send one single-line JSON request envelope per stdin line. Do not send formatted YAML or a single `type: batch` envelope; batch envelopes are rejected with `unsupported_batch_envelope`.

  ## PowerShell.MCP Command Routing
  For every PowerShell Core (`pwsh`) invocation on every operating system:
  - Use PowerShell.MCP 1.14.0 or newer from PSGallery as the command runner. Install or update it with `Install-PSResource PowerShell.MCP` when the agent environment does not provide a current version.
  - `execute_command` is the primary MCP tool for PowerShell cmdlets, CLI tools, navigation, builds, tests, file-system work, and process management. Do not use the removed `invoke_expression` name. Host-qualified names depend on the configured server key: for example, `mcp__powershell__execute_command` for `powershell` and `mcp__pwsh__execute_command` for `pwsh`.
  - Calling `start_console` first is optional because `execute_command` auto-starts or reuses a console. Call `start_console` explicitly only to pre-warm at `start_location`, show a banner, allocate a sub-agent console, or force an additional console by supplying `reason`; omit `reason` when reuse is preferred.
  - Use `get_current_location` when the current PowerShell context matters. For a sub-agent, call `start_console` with `is_subagent=true`, retain the returned `agent_id`, and pass it on every later PowerShell.MCP tool call.
  - When a command continues after the call returns, use `wait_for_completion` to retrieve the cached result instead of running `Start-Sleep`. Use `cancel` for an interruptible pipeline or native CLI, and `close_console` for a non-interruptible command or PowerShell host prompt. If `close_console` reports that a human is typing, only repeat the same PID call when confirming that the console should be closed.
  - In 1.14.0, blocking timeouts are end-to-end deadlines and are capped at 170 seconds for Claude Code and 50 seconds for other or unidentified clients unless a lower limit applies. A timed-out command keeps running and its result is cached for a later tool call.
  - Route `pwsh` commands through a PowerShell.MCP session instead of launching ad hoc PowerShell processes. On Windows, reuse one session for the workspace and route `node` invocations through it as well.
  - When PowerShell.MCP must launch PowerShell Core directly, invoke `pwsh.exe` with `-NoProfile -NonInteractive`. Do not use `powershell.exe`.
  - The PowerShell escape character is the backtick `` ` ``, not the backslash. Never use C or bash-style `\"` escaping inside PowerShell command strings.
  - Prefer single-quoted PowerShell strings for literal regex, paths, JSON/YAML snippets, and text containing pipeline characters such as `|`.
  - When a command needs nested quoting, choose one of these patterns before improvising: `-File` with explicit arguments; piping stdin to the called tool or script; single-quoted or double-quoted here-strings; `-EncodedCommand` for complex inline PowerShell; or correct backtick escaping for embedded PowerShell quotes.
  - If a regex or literal argument contains `|`, `&`, `;`, parentheses, braces, or quotes, verify it is inside a single PowerShell argument before running.
  - For text reads and edits inside PowerShell.MCP, use `Show-TextFiles`, `Add-LinesToFile`, `Update-LinesInFile`, `Update-MatchInFile`, and `Remove-LinesFromFile`; pass literal content through `var1` to `var4`. Version 1.12.0 and newer stage replacements beside the target, so do not apply the obsolete same-volume `TEMP`/`TMP` workaround. Re-read or diff every edit before claiming it landed.
  ## Byrd Development Process
  `Byrd Dev Process`, `BDP`, `BPDv4`, and `Byrd Development Process` refer to `F:\GitHub\McpServer\docs\Development-Process-draft-v4.md`.

  ## Federation Topology
  - To identify hub/proxy topology, call the supported federation status surface, preferably through your required plugin or client wrapper: `/mcpserver/federation/status`. - Status fields to report when relevant: `role`, `configuredRole`, `hubBaseUrl`, `proxyId`, `proxyCount`, `hostedWorkspaceCount`, `queueDepth`, `fanoutDepth`, `conflictCount`, and `staleReadStatus`. - `Standalone` serves local workspaces only. `DirectProxy` is the existing point-to-point proxy mode. `Hub` is authoritative for enrolled proxies and global workspace inventory. `LocalProxy` forwards MCP requests to `hubBaseUrl` and queues mutating requests during hub outages. - LocalProxy queued writes return `202 Accepted` with `X-Mcp-Queued: true` and `X-Mcp-Operation-Id`. Treat the write as optimistic until the hub acknowledges it. - If `queueDepth`, `fanoutDepth`, `conflictCount`, or stale-read status is non-zero/non-clear, include that in session log status and avoid claiming federation synchronization is complete.

  ## Per User Message
  1. Post a new session log turn before starting work.
  2. Complete the user's request.
  3. Update the turn with results and actions when done.

  ## Re-run Full Session Start Only If
  - The user explicitly says "Start Session". - Signature verification fails. - /health fails. - /health nonce verification fails. - Any /mcpserver/* call returns 401. - The marker endpoint/key changes after a server restart.

  ## Continuing After a Server Restart
  The workspace API key rotates on every server restart, so an in-flight agent will begin seeing 401 on /mcpserver/* calls. When that happens, resume through your required agent plugin - do not hand-roll raw REST for session, TODO, or requirements work:
  1. Treat the first 401 (or a /health failure) as a restart signal and stop using the cached API key immediately.
  2. Re-read this marker file (AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml) for the rotated apiKey and current endpoints.
  3. Re-verify trust before resuming: recompute the marker signature with the new key and call /health with a fresh nonce.
  4. Re-bootstrap and resume through your required agent plugin. Codex: run `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Status` to re-establish marker trust, health nonce, workspace, and the current session/turn, then continue with `Invoke-CodexMcpPlugin.ps1 -Command Invoke -Method <method> -Params <yaml>`. Other agents: re-run the plugin session-start hook/command, then continue via the plugin session tools.
  5. Recover the open turn instead of starting over: query session history through the plugin (workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory), find the in-progress turn, then keep updating and complete it via the plugin. Do not open a duplicate session for the same work.
  5a. Treat `deprecated: true` on successful `workflow.*` results as metadata, not wrapper failure. Treat an empty `workflow.sessionlog.queryHistory` result as a valid no-match result. Re-check the workspace current directory, explicit `agent` or `sourceType`, and plugin cache/session state through the wrapper; do not use raw REST merely because history is empty or marked deprecated.
  6. If the plugin cannot re-establish trust after the restart, record `MCP_PLUGIN_UNAVAILABLE:<Agent>` and continue with non-MCP local diagnosis only.

  ## Rules
  0. NEVER write to TODO.yaml directly.
  1. Generate SessionId values using `session.init` (REPL) or `New-McpSessionLogSlug -Agent <SourceType> -Model <Model>` (PowerShell module), then create session logs with `session.new` (REPL) or `New-McpSessionLog -SessionId` (PowerShell). Do not handcraft SessionId values.
  1a. Agents must identify themselves accurately in session logs. `sourceType` and the SessionId `<Agent>` prefix must use the agent's real identity in Pascal-Case. Do not use lowercase forms, placeholders, or legacy aliases.
  2. Post a new session log turn (`session.turn.add` for REPL or `Add-McpSessionTurn` for PowerShell) before starting work. Update it with results (`Response`) and actions (`Add-McpAction` / `session.action.add`) when done. Persist after each meaningful update, not just at the end.
  2a. Before any compaction step, persist the current session log state. After compaction, update the session log again to record the compaction outcome and recovered context.
  3. If signature verification, the /health request, or nonce verification fails, log `MCP_UNTRUSTED`, continue without the MCP server, and do not probe additional MCP endpoints.
  4. Marker signatures use HMAC-SHA256 with the workspace API key in this file as the verifier. Recompute the canonical payload exactly as described by the marker metadata before trusting the file.
  5. Use your required agent plugin for session log, TODO, requirements, import/export, and traceability operations. Do not use raw API calls or generic helper paths except for read-only diagnosis after plugin failure.
  6. Write decisions, requirements, and state to the session log, not just conversation. Capture rich turn detail: interpretation, response/status, actions (type/status/filePath), contextList, filesModified, designDecisions, requirementsDiscovered, blockers, and key processingDialog updates.
  7. Follow workspace conventions in AGENTS.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md.
  8. When you need API schemas, module examples, or compliance rules, load them from docs/context/ or use context_search.
  9. Do not fabricate information. Acknowledge mistakes. Distinguish facts from speculation.
  10. Prioritize correctness over speed. Do not ship code you have not verified compiles.

  11. Use the Byrd Development Process V4 for all plans: organize work into small gated implementation slices, define validation before broadening scope, and keep session-log/TODO updates current between meaningful steps. A Byrd gate requires 100% test success before moving to the next iteration: zero failed tests and zero skipped tests in the executed validation scope. Tests are the progress ledger; do not hide unfinished work with skipped tests. Track deferred scope in MCP TODO/requirements and add its tests when that slice begins.

  ## Commit Signing
  ALL COMMITS MUST BE SIGNED WITH `model-effort@agent` and Model's Confidence in the Correctness, Accuracy, and Completeness of the commit's contents.

  ## Planning Standard
  Plans are frontier-model handoff artifacts. Write them so a less expensive implementation model can execute successfully without resolving unstated product, architecture, interface, data, testing, rollout, or validation decisions.
  Every plan must be decision-complete. Lock the intended behavior, public interfaces, data shapes, migration/backfill strategy, failure modes, rollout or deployment path, validation commands, and acceptance criteria before implementation starts.
  Every plan must capture requirements before implementation: create or update FR/TR/TEST records through the required MCP requirements workflow, include the requirement IDs in the TODO and session log, and map FR to TR and TEST coverage.
  Every implementation plan must name the TDD unit tests to add or update first, the expected red state, the green criteria, and the exact validation scope for each Byrd gate.

  ## Naming Conventions

  - Persisted TODO IDs must be uppercase canonical ids in either <SDLC-PHASE>-<AREA>-### form (regex: ^[A-Z]+-[A-Z0-9]+-\d{3}$) or ISSUE-{number} form (regex: ^ISSUE-\d+$).
  - Valid TODO IDs: PLAN-NAMINGCONVENTIONS-001, MCP-API-042, ISSUE-17.
  - Invalid TODO IDs: plan-api-001, MCP-API-42, ISSUE-ABC, MCPAPI001.
  - Create requests may use ISSUE-NEW only when the intent is to create a new GitHub-backed TODO. The server will create the GitHub issue immediately and persist the TODO using the canonical ISSUE-{number} id.
  - Session IDs must use <Agent>-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<suffix> and start with the exact agent/source type prefix.
  - `<Agent>` / `sourceType` must be the agent's real identity in Pascal-Case. Valid example: `Codex`. Invalid examples: `codex`, `copilotcli` (when the agent is Codex), `Assistant`.
  - Valid Session ID: Copilot-20260304T113901Z-namingconv.
  - Invalid Session IDs: copilot-20260304T113901Z-namingconv, Copilot-2026-03-04-namingconv.
  - Request IDs must use req-<yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<slugOrOrdinal> and be unique within a session.
  - Valid Request ID: req-20260304T113901Z-plan-namingconventions-001.
  - Invalid Request IDs: req-plan-namingconventions-001, request-20260304T113901Z-task-01.

  ## Workspace

  - Name: wordpairs
  - Path: <repo>
  - Primary: False
  - Data Directory: <repo>
  - Todo Path: docs/todo.yaml


  ## Authentication

  All /mcpserver/* endpoints require a per-workspace auth token:
  - Header: X-Api-Key: [REDACTED]
  - Or query param: ?api_key=[REDACTED]
  If you receive a 401, re-read this marker file — the token rotates on each server restart.

  ## Where Things Live

  - AGENTS.md — agent conduct, requirements tracking, session continuity, glossary
  - .github/copilot-instructions.md — build/test commands, architecture, coding conventions
  - docs/context/ — on-demand reference (schemas, module docs, compliance rules, action types)
  - docs/Project/ — requirements docs, TODO.yaml, mapping matrices
  - templates/ — prompt templates

  ## Context Loading by Task Type

  - Session logging → docs/context/session-log-schema.md + docs/context/module-bootstrap.md (pull module-bootstrap via MCP context)
  - TODO management → docs/context/todo-schema.md + docs/context/module-bootstrap.md (pull module-bootstrap via MCP context)
  - API integration → docs/context/api-capabilities.md (or GET http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147/swagger/v1/swagger.json)
  - Adding dependencies → docs/context/compliance-rules.md
  - Logging actions → docs/context/action-types.md

  ## Protocols

  - REST API: http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147/mcpserver/* (requires X-Api-Key). Use this for typed client/API integration and read-only diagnosis after the required plugin/tool route fails. Do not bypass the required plugin for session log, TODO, requirements, import/export, or traceability operations. Swagger UI: http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147/swagger
  - MCP Streamable HTTP: POST http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147/mcp-transport (no API key required)
  - Health: GET http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147/health

  ## Repository Access

  - Hosted agents expose built-in repository tools: `mcp_repo_list`, `mcp_repo_read`, and `mcp_repo_write`.
  - All repository paths are relative to <home>/github/WordGame/.mcpServer/wordpairs.
  - REST clients can browse and edit files through http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147/mcpserver/repo/list and http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147/mcpserver/repo/file using the API key above.
  - If you need to browse or edit files, use these repository tools instead of saying that filesystem access is unavailable.
  ## Local Program Execution

  - Hosted agents expose a built-in local program execution tool: `mcp_desktop_launch`.
  - Use it when you need to start a local Windows program through MCP Server instead of claiming local program execution is unavailable.
  - Prefer `createNoWindow: true` and `waitForExit: true` for short non-interactive verification commands.
  - REST clients can launch programs through http://[PRIVATE HOST]:7147/mcpserver/desktop/launch using the API key above.





  ## Before Delivering Output

  Verify: session log is current, decisions are recorded, requirements are tracked, code compiles, action types are correct (see docs/context/action-types.md).

  ## Available Capabilities

  The following core libraries are indexed and available for semantic search/context retrieval:
  - McpServer.Cqrs (CQRS framework)
  - McpServer.Cqrs.Mvvm (MVVM support)

    [string]$Id = '',
    [string]$FrId = '',
    [string]$TrId = '',
    [string]$TestId = ''

if ($Id) { $params['id'] = $Id }
if ($FrId) { $params['frId'] = $FrId }
if ($TrId) { $params['trId'] = $TrId }
if ($TestId) { $params['testId'] = $TestId }
$yaml = if ($params.Count) { ConvertTo-Yaml $params } else { '{}' }

$exit = $LASTEXITCODE

    params   = $params
    exitCode = $exit
    lines    = @($output).Count
    path     = $path

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$IndexPath = '<repo>/docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/round6-frozen-evidence-3fb4a49/evidence-index.json'
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

function Get-Sha {
    param([string]$Path)
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return 'MISSING' }
    return (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $Path -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
}

function Get-JUnitSummary {
    param([string]$Path)
    [xml]$doc = Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Raw
    $cases = @($doc.SelectNodes('//testcase'))
    $failed = @($cases | Where-Object { $_.SelectSingleNode('failure') -or $_.SelectSingleNode('error') }).Count
    $skipped = @($cases | Where-Object { $_.SelectSingleNode('skipped') }).Count
    $names = @($cases | ForEach-Object { ([string]$_.classname + ' :: ' + [string]$_.name).Trim() })
    $suites = @($doc.SelectNodes('//testsuite'))
    $stamps = @($suites | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.GetAttribute('timestamp') } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    [pscustomobject]@{ cases = $cases.Count; failed = $failed; skipped = $skipped; names = $names; uniqueNames = @($names | Sort-Object -Unique).Count; timestamps = $stamps; testNames = @($cases | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.name }) }
}

function Get-TrxSummary {
    param([string]$Path)
    [xml]$doc = Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Raw
    $ns = [System.Xml.XmlNamespaceManager]::new($doc.NameTable)
    $ns.AddNamespace('t', 'http://microsoft.com/schemas/VisualStudio/TeamTest/2010')
    $results = @($doc.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTestResult', $ns))
    $outcomes = $results | Group-Object { [string]$_.outcome } | ForEach-Object { $_.Name + '=' + $_.Count }
    $counters = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:ResultSummary/t:Counters', $ns)
    $summaryOutcome = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:ResultSummary', $ns)
    $times = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:Times', $ns)
    $runId = [string]$doc.DocumentElement.GetAttribute('id')
    $runName = [string]$doc.DocumentElement.GetAttribute('name')
    [pscustomobject]@{
        results       = $results.Count
        outcomes      = @($outcomes) -join ','
        counters      = if ($counters) { 'total=' + $counters.total + ' executed=' + $counters.executed + ' passed=' + $counters.passed + ' failed=' + $counters.failed + ' notExecuted=' + $counters.notExecuted } else { 'none' }
        summary       = if ($summaryOutcome) { [string]$summaryOutcome.outcome } else { 'none' }
        times         = if ($times) { 'creation=' + $times.creation + ' start=' + $times.start + ' finish=' + $times.finish } else { 'none' }
        runId         = $runId
        runName       = $runName
        testNames     = @($results | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.testName })
    }
}

$index = Get-Content -LiteralPath $IndexPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
'INDEX=' + $IndexPath + ' SHA=' + (Get-Sha $IndexPath)
'MANIFEST=' + $index.sourceManifest + ' recorded=' + $index.sourceManifestSha256 + ' actual=' + (Get-Sha $index.sourceManifest)
foreach ($r in $index.reports) {
    $junitActual = Get-Sha $r.junit
    $trxActual = Get-Sha $r.trx
    $j = Get-JUnitSummary $r.junit
    $t = Get-TrxSummary $r.trx
    $jSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$j.testNames)
    $tSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$t.testNames)
    $onlyJ = @($j.testNames | Where-Object { -not $tSet.Contains($_) } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    $onlyT = @($t.testNames | Where-Object { -not $jSet.Contains($_) } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    $runLine = ''
    $runProps = $r.run.PSObject.Properties.Name
    if ($runProps -contains 'trx') {
        $runTrxActual = Get-Sha $r.run.trx
        $runJunitActual = Get-Sha $r.run.junit
        $rt = Get-TrxSummary $r.run.trx
        $runLine = ' | runTrx recorded=' + $r.run.trxSha256.Substring(0, 8) + ' actual=' + $runTrxActual.Substring(0, 8) + ' match=' + ($r.run.trxSha256 -eq $runTrxActual) + ' runTrxResults=' + $rt.results + ' runTrxOutcomes=' + $rt.outcomes + ' runTrxTimes=' + $rt.times + ' runTrxRunId=' + $rt.runId + ' | runJunit match=' + ($r.run.junitSha256 -eq $runJunitActual)
    }
    $producer = ''
    if ($runProps -contains 'producerSha256') {
        $script = $r.run.arguments[3]
        $producer = ' | producer ' + $script + ' recorded=' + $r.run.producerSha256.Substring(0, 8) + ' actual=' + (Get-Sha $script).Substring(0, 8) + ' match=' + ($r.run.producerSha256 -eq (Get-Sha $script))
    }
    ('{0}: junit match={1} ({2}) trx match={3} ({4}) | junit cases={5} failed={6} skipped={7} unique={8} stamps={9} | trx results={10} outcomes={11} counters=[{12}] summary={13} times=[{14}] trxRunId={15} | onlyJUnit={16} onlyTrx={17} | index cases={18} failed={19} skipped={20} exit={21} runId={22} rev={23} {24}-{25}{26}{27}' -f
        $r.name, ($r.junitSha256 -eq $junitActual), $junitActual.Substring(0, 8), ($r.trxSha256 -eq $trxActual), $trxActual.Substring(0, 8),
        $j.cases, $j.failed, $j.skipped, $j.uniqueNames, ($j.timestamps -join ';'),
        $t.results, $t.outcomes, $t.counters, $t.summary, $t.times, $t.runId,
        $onlyJ.Count, $onlyT.Count, $r.cases, $r.failed, $r.skipped, $r.run.exitCode, $r.run.runId, $r.run.revision.Substring(0, 7), $r.run.startedAt, $r.run.finishedAt, $runLine, $producer)
    if ($j.cases -le 12) { '  junit names: ' + ($j.names -join ' || ') }
    $dups = @($j.names | Group-Object | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | ForEach-Object { $_.Name + ' x' + $_.Count })
    if ($dups.Count) { '  duplicate junit names: ' + ($dups -join ' || ') }
}
'AT=' + (Get-Date -Format s)

    $suites = @($doc.SelectNodes('//testsuite'))
    $stamps = @($suites | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.GetAttribute('timestamp') } | Where-Object { $_ } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    [pscustomobject]@{ cases = $cases.Count; failed = $failed; skipped = $skipped; names = $names; uniqueNames = @($names | Sort-Object -Unique).Count; timestamps = $stamps; testNames = @($cases | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.name }) }
}

function Get-TrxSummary {
    param([string]$Path)
    [xml]$doc = Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Raw
    $ns = [System.Xml.XmlNamespaceManager]::new($doc.NameTable)
    $ns.AddNamespace('t', 'http://microsoft.com/schemas/VisualStudio/TeamTest/2010')
    $results = @($doc.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTestResult', $ns))
    $outcomes = $results | Group-Object { [string]$_.outcome } | ForEach-Object { $_.Name + '=' + $_.Count }
    $counters = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:ResultSummary/t:Counters', $ns)
    $summaryOutcome = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:ResultSummary', $ns)
    $times = $doc.SelectSingleNode('//t:Times', $ns)
    $runId = [string]$doc.DocumentElement.GetAttribute('id')
    $runName = [string]$doc.DocumentElement.GetAttribute('name')
    [pscustomobject]@{
        results       = $results.Count
        outcomes      = @($outcomes) -join ','
        counters      = if ($counters) { 'total=' + $counters.total + ' executed=' + $counters.executed + ' passed=' + $counters.passed + ' failed=' + $counters.failed + ' notExecuted=' + $counters.notExecuted } else { 'none' }
        summary       = if ($summaryOutcome) { [string]$summaryOutcome.outcome } else { 'none' }
        times         = if ($times) { 'creation=' + $times.creation + ' start=' + $times.start + ' finish=' + $times.finish } else { 'none' }
        runId         = $runId
        runName       = $runName
        testNames     = @($results | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.testName })
    }
}

$index = Get-Content -LiteralPath $IndexPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
'INDEX=' + $IndexPath + ' SHA=' + (Get-Sha $IndexPath)
'MANIFEST=' + $index.sourceManifest + ' recorded=' + $index.sourceManifestSha256 + ' actual=' + (Get-Sha $index.sourceManifest)
foreach ($r in $index.reports) {
    $junitActual = Get-Sha $r.junit
    $trxActual = Get-Sha $r.trx
    $j = Get-JUnitSummary $r.junit
    $t = Get-TrxSummary $r.trx
    $jSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$j.testNames)
    $tSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$t.testNames)
    $onlyJ = @($j.testNames | Where-Object { -not $tSet.Contains($_) } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    $onlyT = @($t.testNames | Where-Object { -not $jSet.Contains($_) } | Sort-Object -Unique)
    $runLine = ''
    $runProps = $r.run.PSObject.Properties.Name
    if ($runProps -contains 'trx') {
        $runTrxActual = Get-Sha $r.run.trx
        $runJunitActual = Get-Sha $r.run.junit
        $rt = Get-TrxSummary $r.run.trx
        $runLine = ' | runTrx recorded=' + $r.run.trxSha256.Substring(0, 8) + ' actual=' + $runTrxActual.Substring(0, 8) + ' match=' + ($r.run.trxSha256 -eq $runTrxActual) + ' runTrxResults=' + $rt.results + ' runTrxOutcomes=' + $rt.outcomes + ' runTrxTimes=' + $rt.times + ' runTrxRunId=' + $rt.runId + ' | runJunit match=' + ($r.run.junitSha256 -eq $runJunitActual)
    }
    $producer = ''
    if ($runProps -contains 'producerSha256') {
        $script = $r.run.arguments[3]
        $producer = ' | producer ' + $script + ' recorded=' + $r.run.producerSha256.Substring(0, 8) + ' actual=' + (Get-Sha $script).Substring(0, 8) + ' match=' + ($r.run.producerSha256 -eq (Get-Sha $script))
    }
    ('{0}: junit match={1} ({2}) trx match={3} ({4}) | junit cases={5} failed={6} skipped={7} unique={8} stamps={9} | trx results={10} outcomes={11} counters=[{12}] summary={13} times=[{14}] trxRunId={15} | onlyJUnit={16} onlyTrx={17} | index cases={18} failed={19} skipped={20} exit={21} runId={22} rev={23} {24}-{25}{26}{27}' -f
        $r.name, ($r.junitSha256 -eq $junitActual), $junitActual.Substring(0, 8), ($r.trxSha256 -eq $trxActual), $trxActual.Substring(0, 8),
        $j.cases, $j.failed, $j.skipped, $j.uniqueNames, ($j.timestamps -join ';'),
        $t.results, $t.outcomes, $t.counters, $t.summary, $t.times, $t.runId,
        $onlyJ.Count, $onlyT.Count, $r.cases, $r.failed, $r.skipped, $r.run.exitCode, $r.run.runId, $r.run.revision.Substring(0, 7), $r.run.startedAt, $r.run.finishedAt, $runLine, $producer)
    if ($j.cases -le 12) { '  junit names: ' + ($j.names -join ' || ') }
    $dups = @($j.names | Group-Object | Where-Object Count -gt 1 | ForEach-Object { $_.Name + ' x' + $_.Count })
    if ($dups.Count) { '  duplicate junit names: ' + ($dups -join ' || ') }
}

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]$IndexPath = '<repo>/docs/evidence/hosting/guest-admin-recovery/round6-frozen-evidence-3fb4a49/evidence-index.json'
)

Set-StrictMode -Version Latest
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$index = Get-Content -LiteralPath $IndexPath -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
foreach ($r in $index.reports) {
    [xml]$j = Get-Content -LiteralPath $r.junit -Raw
    [xml]$t = Get-Content -LiteralPath $r.trx -Raw
    $ns = [System.Xml.XmlNamespaceManager]::new($t.NameTable)
    $ns.AddNamespace('t', 'http://microsoft.com/schemas/VisualStudio/TeamTest/2010')
    $jNames = @($j.SelectNodes('//testcase') | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.name })
    $jFull = @($j.SelectNodes('//testcase') | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.classname + '.' + [string]$_.name })
    $tNames = @($t.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTestResult', $ns) | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.testName })
    $tDefs = @($t.SelectNodes('//t:UnitTest/t:TestMethod', $ns) | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.className + '.' + [string]$_.name })
    $sample = if ($tNames.Count) { $tNames[0] } else { '' }
    $bestMissing = [int]::MaxValue
    $bestForm = ''
    foreach ($form in @('name', 'full', 'defs')) {
        $left = switch ($form) { 'name' { $jNames } 'full' { $jFull } 'defs' { $jFull } }
        $right = switch ($form) { 'name' { $tNames } 'full' { $tNames } 'defs' { $tDefs } }
        $rightSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$right)
        $leftSet = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([string[]]$left)
        $missing = @($left | Where-Object { -not $rightSet.Contains($_) }).Count + @($right | Where-Object { -not $leftSet.Contains($_) }).Count
        if ($missing -lt $bestMissing) { $bestMissing = $missing; $bestForm = $form }
    }
    ('{0}: junit={1} trxResults={2} trxDefs={3} bestForm={4} oneSided={5} sampleTrxName={6}' -f $r.name, $jNames.Count, $tNames.Count, $tDefs.Count, $bestForm, $bestMissing, $sample)
}
'AT=' + (Get-Date -Format s)

# Reaction test failure analysis

This record distinguishes observed results from explanations that remain unproven. The historical error-context files named in the logs were not preserved; the test-results directory was subsequently reused. They cannot be reconstructed. The original logs and JUnit reports remain alongside their receipts.

The full `round4-candidate` browser run failed the pre-boundary `toBeDisabled` assertion: the control was enabled when the test expected it to be disabled. The test installed a running browser clock, advanced fixture server time by 1,999 ms, and fast-forwarded each page. The original cause is unproven. A running clock and independent server-time advance are plausible contributors, but the retained log does not establish either as the cause. Three later repetitions of the unchanged case passed; they do not explain the earlier failure.

The four subsequent experiments used the same focused command, `npm exec playwright -- test tests/browser/reactions.phase5.spec.ts --config=playwright.pwa.config.ts --repeat-each=3 --reporter=line,junit`, on [PRIVATE HOST] with the local browser and fixture server. Their individual receipt files preserve the spec hashes, local end timestamps, revision labels, and exit codes. These earlier runs did not generate unique run IDs or independently record their start times; neither can be reconstructed. The revision labels identify the then-current Git HEAD, not the uncommitted test bytes, which are identified by the recorded hashes and log excerpts.

- `reaction-round5-clock`: install and pause the same initial time, then use `fastForward`. Three of three runs failed because the control remained disabled at the later assertion. Inference: jumping the paused clock can skip intermediate interval callbacks; this log alone does not prove the mechanism.
- `reaction-round5-clock-v2`: use `runFor` but advance the server fixture by 1,999 ms before browser timers. Three of three runs failed because the control was enabled before the expected boundary. Inference: a refresh could observe the fixture's advanced server time while browser time was still advancing; the retained log does not prove the sequence.
- `reaction-round5-clock-v3`: advance the server and paused browser clocks in steps. Two runs passed; one failed before navigation with `clock.pauseAt: Cannot fast-forward to the past`. Inference: time elapsed between installing and pausing the clock at the same timestamp.
- `reaction-round5-clock-v4`: install one minute before the target, pause at the target, and advance server and browser clocks in steps. All three runs passed. The identical spec hash appears in `reaction-round5-repeat25`, where 25 runs passed, and in the subsequent full source-pinned suite. These results do not establish the cause of the original failure.

The browser observes the cooldown through a 250 ms display timer. The component test in `tests/web/social-panel.test.ts` independently checks the control with supplied values at 1,999 ms and 2,000 ms. Neither local fixture proves hosted delivery or physical-device behavior.

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$ReportDirectory)
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
$repo=Split-Path $PSScriptRoot
$report=[IO.Path]::GetFullPath($ReportDirectory)
if(-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($report,'Run isolated PowerShell contracts and write JUnit evidence')){return}
$null=New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $report -Force
$revision=(& git -C $repo rev-parse HEAD).Trim()
$runId=[Guid]::NewGuid().ToString('D')
$started=Get-Date -Format s
$results=[Collections.Generic.List[object]]::new()
foreach($name in @('local-live-lease.contract.ps1','local-realtime-cleanup.contract.ps1','local-ui-startup.contract.ps1')){
 $path=Join-Path $repo "tests/integration/$name"
 $arguments=@('-NoProfile','-NonInteractive','-File',$path)
 $caseStart=Get-Date -Format s
 & pwsh @arguments *>&1 | Tee-Object (Join-Path $report "$name.log")
 $results.Add([pscustomobject]@{name=$name;runId=$runId;hostName=[Environment]::MachineName;revision=$revision;startedAt=$caseStart;finishedAt=(Get-Date -Format s);executable='pwsh';arguments=$arguments;exitCode=$LASTEXITCODE;sha256=(Get-FileHash $path).Hash})
}
$doc=[System.Xml.XmlDocument]::new()
$suite=$doc.CreateElement('testsuite')
$suite.SetAttribute('name','isolated PowerShell contracts')
$suite.SetAttribute('tests',[string]$results.Count)
$failed=@($results|Where-Object exitCode -ne 0).Count
$suite.SetAttribute('failures',[string]$failed)
$null=$doc.AppendChild($suite)
foreach($result in $results){
 $case=$doc.CreateElement('testcase');$case.SetAttribute('classname','local-script-contract');$case.SetAttribute('name',$result.name)
 if($result.exitCode -ne 0){$failure=$doc.CreateElement('failure');$failure.SetAttribute('message',"Exit code $($result.exitCode); see $($result.name).log");$null=$case.AppendChild($failure)}
 $null=$suite.AppendChild($case)
}
$doc.Save((Join-Path $report 'contracts.xml'))
[pscustomobject]@{runId=$runId;hostName=[Environment]::MachineName;revision=$revision;startedAt=$started;finishedAt=(Get-Date -Format s);producer=$PSCommandPath;producerSha256=(Get-FileHash $PSCommandPath).Hash;invocation=@('pwsh','-NoProfile','-NonInteractive','-File',$PSCommandPath,'-ReportDirectory',$report);results=@($results)}|ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8|Set-Content (Join-Path $report 'contracts.json')
if($failed){throw "$failed local script contracts failed."}

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$ReportDirectory)
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
$root=(Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '../..')).ProviderPath
$test=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.Tests.ps1'
$correct=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockCorrect.psm1'
$wrong=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockWrong.psm1'
$wrongEmpty=Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'HostingSchemaPlanner.MockWrongEmpty.psm1'
if(-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($ReportDirectory,'Run independent planner mock gate and save evidence')){return}
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ReportDirectory -Force|Out-Null
$runs=@()
foreach($case in @(@{name='correct';module=$correct},@{name='wrong';module=$wrong},@{name='wrong-empty';module=$wrongEmpty})){
    $env:WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE=$case.module
    $configuration=New-PesterConfiguration
    $configuration.Run.Path=@($test)
    $configuration.Run.PassThru=$true
    $configuration.Output.Verbosity='Detailed'
    $configuration.TestResult.Enabled=$true
    $configuration.TestResult.OutputFormat='NUnitXml'
    $configuration.TestResult.OutputPath=Join-Path $ReportDirectory ($case.name+'.xml')
    $result=Invoke-Pester -Configuration $configuration
    $cases=@($result.Tests | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{name=$_.Name;result=[string]$_.Result} })
    $runs+= [pscustomobject]@{name=$case.name;passed=$result.PassedCount;failed=$result.FailedCount;skipped=$result.SkippedCount;cases=$cases}
}
Remove-Item Env:WORDPAIRS_PLANNER_MODULE -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if($runs[0].passed -ne 6 -or $runs[0].failed -ne 0 -or $runs[0].skipped -ne 0){throw 'Correct mock did not pass every planner case.'}
foreach($case in $runs[0].cases){
    $controls=@($runs[1..2] | ForEach-Object { $_.cases | Where-Object name -CEQ $case.name })
    if($controls.Count -ne 2 -or @($controls | Where-Object result -EQ 'Failed').Count -eq 0){throw "No rejecting negative control for: $($case.name)"}
}
$receipt=[pscustomobject]@{
    timestamp=Get-Date -Format s
    root=$root
    test=(Resolve-Path $test).ProviderPath
    testSha256=(Get-FileHash $test -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    correctMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $correct -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    wrongMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $wrong -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    wrongEmptyMockSha256=(Get-FileHash $wrongEmpty -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
    runs=$runs
    qualification='Catch-up mock sensitivity check. This receipt does not backdate or replace the original pre-implementation gate.'
}
$receipt|ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6|Set-Content (Join-Path $ReportDirectory 'mock-gate.json')
$receipt|ConvertTo-Json -Depth 6

#Requires -Version 7.0
[CmdletBinding(SupportsShouldProcess)]
param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$ReportDirectory)
$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
if(-not $PSCmdlet.ShouldProcess($ReportDirectory,'Run documentation drift checks and write JUnit evidence')){return}
$null=New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $ReportDirectory -Force
$repo=Split-Path $PSScriptRoot
$config=New-PesterConfiguration
$config.Run.Path=@(Join-Path $repo 'tests/powershell/CurrentReleaseDocs.Tests.ps1')
$config.Run.PassThru=$true
$config.Output.Verbosity='Normal'
$config.TestResult.Enabled=$true
$config.TestResult.OutputFormat='JUnitXml'
$config.TestResult.OutputPath=Join-Path $ReportDirectory 'docs.xml'
$result=Invoke-Pester -Configuration $config
if($result.PassedCount -ne 6 -or $result.FailedCount -or $result.SkippedCount){throw 'Documentation drift tests failed or did not all run.'}

 ## 4. Roles and permissions
 
-The 27 October 2026 [admin/ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md) makes the roles operational. Its permission matrix supersedes the earlier proposed separation between moderator and content-editor accounts below: moderators and senior moderators can curate approved cases and author/edit catalog pairs; administrators additionally manage role grants and revocations. Direct editorial saves require a reason and create immutable versions. Community case review and independent appeals remain mandatory for the community workflow. The admin role does not waive proposer/original-reviewer independence.
+Historical design: the 27 October 2026 [admin/ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md) described delegated moderation and administration. The current release instead uses the fixed-owner GitHub administrator described in [the release record](admin_pwa_release.md); community submissions and role delegation are inactive. The table below records the earlier policy, not current access.
 
-Bootstrap administrators are defined by the server-only `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` allowlist. Other privileges are persisted in PostgreSQL, audited and checked on the server. Configured administrator authority cannot be removed through the UI, and concurrent changes cannot remove every effective administrator. There is no public privilege-escalation or role-bootstrap endpoint.
+Historically, bootstrap administrators used a server-only profile-ID allowlist and persisted audited grants. This is not an authorization path for the current release.
 
 | Role | Allowed actions | Not allowed |
 |---|---|---|
 | Player / submitter | Submit an eligible nomination; submit an unlocked category/pair proposal; view own submission status and public decision reason; submit one appeal to a Senior Moderator. | See another player's private nomination identity, internal reviewer notes, or unresolved drafts; approve own content; edit the live catalog. |
 | Moderator | Review eligible cases; approve or reject with a reason; curate complete approved proposals; author/edit word pairs and hints as immutable versions; exclude content from future rounds; inspect content history. | Change vote history or scores, approve own submission, resolve appeals, assign roles, or erase audit history. |
 | Senior moderator | All moderator permissions plus independent reasoned appeal resolution. | Resolve an appeal of own submission or original decision, assign roles, or erase audit history. |
-| Administrator | All senior-moderator permissions plus audited role grants/revocations and user-directory access. | Bypass proposer/original-reviewer independence, remove configured administrator authority through the UI, remove the final effective administrator, or erase audit history. |
+| Administrator (historical policy) | All senior-moderator permissions plus audited role grants/revocations and user-directory access. | Bypass proposer/original-reviewer independence, remove configured administrator authority through the UI, remove the final effective administrator, or erase audit history. |
 | System | Validate structure, normalize duplicate keys, count eligible votes/wins, create queue cases, enforce status transitions, and record immutable events. | Make final content suitability decisions unless a specific deterministic rule has been approved. |
 
 The landing page uses generated public aliases and honors profile opt-out as specified in v2.6. Do not expose moderator-only fields or nomination histories as leaderboard data. If player-selected labels are used publicly, the display-name policy must define reserved/prohibited strings, report/removal handling, and how a disabled label is represented. These choices belong to the landing-page decision register, not the nomination review queue unless the product owner explicitly connects the workflows.

 | `WORDPAIRS_DATABASE_URL` | Private PostgreSQL application connection. The runtime always verifies TLS certificates and rejects URL options that override its TLS configuration. |
 | `WORDPAIRS_DATABASE_CA` | Optional PEM CA contents for a database with a private/local certificate authority. Supply the CA rather than disabling certificate verification. |
 | `WORDPAIRS_INVITE_SECRET` | Server invitation-signing secret of at least 32 characters. Generate it from cryptographic random bytes and retain it across restarts. |
-| `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` | Optional comma-separated existing profile IDs that receive administrator authority. See bootstrap below. |
+| `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | Server-only GitHub App credentials for the fixed-owner administrator sign-in. |
 | `WORDPAIRS_SUPABASE_URL`, `WORDPAIRS_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `WORDPAIRS_SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY`, `WORDPAIRS_SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` | Realtime connection, private-channel authorization and outbox delivery configuration. All four are required to construct the Realtime adapter. |
-| `WORDPAIRS_OIDC_ISSUER`, `WORDPAIRS_OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `WORDPAIRS_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` | Optional approved OIDC provider settings. Issuer, client ID and canonical origin enable the provider; a client secret is used when configured. The callback is `/api/auth/callback` on the canonical origin. Guest play does not require OIDC. |

# Wordpairs Architecture Design

Current release scope: [guest-only game and owner-only GitHub admin PWA](admin_pwa_release.md). Configure server-only WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET and the exact canonical origin for administration. Public OpenAI/member sign-in, user delegation, nominations and community-submission UI are inactive. Public pages have no install metadata/controls; admin manifest/worker launch at /admin. Earlier feature counts and provider/delegation instructions below describe their historical snapshots. Current active browser tests use playwright.pwa.config.ts; superseded community cases are retained under docs/testing/historical/.


**Requirements traceability, DDD component split, and design-pattern class views**  
Version 1.1 · 27 October 2026 · Derived from Requirements v2.6 and the administration/ACL extension

This document maps every baseline functional requirement (FR-01–FR-22) and technical requirement (TR-01–TR-31) to bounded contexts, application components and logical classes. Names below describe responsibilities, not mandatory programming-language syntax. Coding Phases 1–6 are complete; the administration extension is documented separately below. Vercel and Supabase/Postgres remain the selected deployment and persistence target (TR-20–TR-24), with hosted deployment work in Phase 7. The implementation is a Next.js/TypeScript modular monolith with the Phase 0-approved interfaces. The diagrams are SVG assets embedded here; the current source layout is documented in [local development](local_development.md).

## Architecture rules

The [phone PWA extension](pwa_design.md) adds a native Next manifest, original install icons, secure root worker registration and browser-controlled installation guidance. Its worker caches only a self-contained offline document and an explicit public icon allowlist. API/authentication/realtime traffic, mutations and private server-rendered/RSC data stay on the network; navigation failures display reconnect guidance. Updates wait for existing app windows to close. No domain, persistence or authorization rules move into the worker.

The [administration and ACL extension](admin_acl_design.md), requested 27 October 2026, adds `/admin`, `/admin/words`, and `/admin/users`, an explicit permission matrix, server-configured bootstrap administrators, serialized role assignment and immutable pair revisions. It extends the implemented baseline without changing historical phase approval receipts. Identity roles are reloaded server-side; UI visibility is never the permission boundary.

- Domain policies contain each business rule once and import no Next.js, React, Supabase, or transport code.
- Application use cases orchestrate domain decisions and ports; route handlers validate/translate transport input and call use cases.
- A room aggregate is the serialization boundary for membership, readiness, countdown, and roster state. A match/round aggregate owns answer progression and scoring.
- Repository transactions, unique/check constraints, row locking or compare-and-swap, idempotency, and transactional outbox writes protect concurrent commands.
- Realtime is delivery, not authority. Clients render authorized projections and may retry with the same command ID.
- Read projections have explicit field allowlists for players, observers, moderators, and the public landing page.
- Clock, randomness, identity verification, deadline scheduling, storage, and event delivery are ports, so domain and use-case tests can use deterministic fakes.

file.content: # Wordpairs Actual game UI with demonstration players. Slides alternate every seven seconds. [Phone view](docs/images/readme/wordpairs-phone-perspective.png) · [Desktop view](docs/images/readme/wordpairs-desktop-perspective.png) · [Capture details](docs/images/readme/capture-receipt.json) Every category has cel-shaded comic backgrounds in **9:16 for phones** and **16:9 for desktop**, displayed behind a frosted translucent game surface. [View all twelve backgrounds and their design](docs/category_artwork.md). Wordpairs is a real-time word-association game. Its [requirements](docs/word_association_game_requirements.md), [AC gap analysis](docs/ac_gap_analysis.md), [test execution receipt](docs/test_execution_receipt.jsonl), [planned AC test inventory](docs/ac_test_inventory.md), [repo review receipt](docs/repo_review_receipt.jsonl), [implementation plan](docs/implementation_plan.md), [Phase 1A execution record](docs/phase1a_execution.md), [Phase 0–6 hostile-validation goal](docs/goal_hv_agreement_through_phase_6.md), [Phase 0 execution tracker](docs/implementation_phase0_execution.md), [Phase 0 interface and data contracts](docs/phase0_interface_and_data_contracts.md), [Phase 0 approval receipt](docs/phase0_approval_receipt.jsonl), [Phase 0 refresh review receipt](docs/phase0_refresh_hostile_review_receipt.jsonl), [implementation kickoff review receipt](docs/implementation_kickoff_receipt.jsonl), [approved architecture decision record](docs/architecture_decision_record.md), [architecture design and FR/TR traceability](docs/architecture_design.md), [architecture patterns](docs/architecture_patterns.md), [deployment plan](docs/deployment_plan.md), [moderation plan](docs/moderation_plan.md), and rendered diagrams are in `docs/`. ## Project status Current change in progress: [guest game and owner-only GitHub admin PWA](docs/admin_pwa_release.md). Staging currently serves the earlier release; this change needs its own reviewed-commit rollout. Phases 0–6 completed implementation and independent phase-exit review, including multiplayer gameplay, moderation and final acceptance. Historical evidence remains in the [Phase 6 execution record](docs/phase6_execution.md). The [administration and ACL extension](docs/admin_acl_design.md) adds dedicated moderation, word/hint editing and role-management pages, with its own validation. Hosted deployment remains Phase 7; a locally running app is not a hosted release. ## Local setup and validation The application uses Next.js 16.4.3, React 19.3.1 and TypeScript 6.0.3, pinned in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`. Install dependencies with `npm ci`, configure the server environment and a migrated TLS-enabled database as described in [local development](docs/local_development.md), then run `npm run dev -- --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3000`. Open the exact origin configured in `WORDPAIRS_ORIGIN`. The [testing guide](docs/testing.md) lists unit, PostgreSQL, multiplayer, administration, Realtime and browser commands and their evidence boundaries. The administration candidate passed 502 unit/contract tests, 66 PostgreSQL tests and 31 browser journeys, plus the production build. Its [independent hostile review](docs/admin_acl_review_receipt.json) approved the recorded [189-file snapshot](docs/admin_acl_review_manifest.json) at 99/100 for accuracy and completeness with no unresolved findings. This documentation refresh follows that snapshot and does not relabel it as a review of later bytes. The [wiki manifest](docs/wiki.yaml) indexes current guides and historical execution records. MCP trust and logging were restored by registering this repository and correcting the service configuration file's ACL mask. The [maintenance receipt](docs/maintenance_receipt.json) records the recovery, triage reports and requirements-export outcome. ## Administration and installation The public game uses guests only and has no account sign-in or PWA install controls. Administration at `/admin` and `/admin/words` uses the registered GitHub App and permits only the verified `sharpninja` account. User delegation and public community submissions/nominations are disabled in this release. Set server-only `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `WORDPAIRS_GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` together with the canonical `WORDPAIRS_ORIGIN`. Both hosting callbacks are registered; GitHub credentials belong in the hosting secret configuration, never source control. Former `WORDPAIRS_ADMIN_PROFILE_IDS` guest/bootstrap grants do not authorize this release's admin routes. Only administration remains installable. Sign into `/admin` over HTTPS, then use **Get Wordpairs Admin on your phone** or the browser's install menu. The manifest launches at `/admin`; its worker caches only generic offline HTML and public icons. Admin/guest sessions are separate and private data is not cached. The former public worker retires itself; an already-installed OS icon requires manual removal if no longer wanted. See the [current release design, cases and QBrain references](docs/admin_pwa_release.md). Earlier [PWA](docs/pwa_design.md) and [ACL](docs/admin_acl_design.md) reviews remain historical evidence. Physical OS installation and live standalone GitHub cookie continuity are separate from automated Chromium installability checks. ## Multiplayer integration tests Run `npm run test:multiplayer` with Docker, PowerShell 7, and installed npm dependencies. The runner creates a disposable, loopback-only PostgreSQL container, applies every migration, and removes the container in `finally`. It does not use the running game's database. The suite plays eight-round games at every size from 2 through 25 players (24 games, 324 player participations). It exercises real identity, room, lobby, match, and PostgreSQL services, including simultaneous answer conflicts and retries, all hint/scoring stages, shared final standings, and exactly-once profile awards. Time and random draws are controlled; browser UI and Realtime transport remain covered by their separate suites. The full `tests/integration/run-phase1.ps1` run also includes this suite. ## License The game is intended to use GNU GPL version 2 only (`GPL-2.0-only`). See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). ## Deployment target The application target is Vercel from `sharpninja/wordpairs`. Coding Phases 1–6 precede all Phase 7 deployment and release work. ## Live multiplayer runtime Live gameplay needs authenticated Realtime configuration and an independent deadline/outbox worker. A rendered page alone does not establish a working game. See [local live setup](docs/local_development.md) and [real browser integration](docs/room_sync_fix.md). `npm run test:live-ui` targets an explicitly configured real runtime and complements the service integration suite. For a repeatable local browser matrix, run `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/run-local-ui-integration.ps1` after a production build. It uses installed Chromium, owned disposable TLS databases on volatile test storage, private Realtime and loopback HTTPS, then cleans up only its owned resources. It does not establish disk durability or public capacity. See [the UI harness guide](docs/testing.md#disposable-loopback-https-ui-harness). ## UI workflow and recovery extension Existing moderation history and immutable word/hint editing remain available to the owner. Multi-account community submission/resubmission and browser role delegation are inactive under the current guest-only release. Their original UI cases remain in `docs/testing/historical/`, while policy/transaction tests stay available. Profile Save/Cancel, safe retries and active game/accessibility journeys remain in the current browser suite. No-solver rounds still advance after the server delay. See the [current release design](docs/admin_pwa_release.md) and [historical UI implementation](docs/testing/ui/implementation.md). Contest readiness and all historical hostile-validation evidence are tracked in [the submission checklist](docs/submission/README.md). The official cutoff is earlier than the public marketing date; final public/live evidence and entrant prerequisites remain explicit.
